criteria.description: Create products, sales and sale_lines with primary/foreign keys in SQLite. Enable PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON on the connection. Save schema.sql and a runnable loader. Mark: implementation/artefact meets stated requirements (6); demonstrated stated cases with actual output (3); explanation of the result (1).

Insert two products and two sales. Add Pen quantities 2 and 3 to separate sales, plus Book quantity 1. Save seed SQL and explain each relationship. Mark: implementation/artefact meets stated requirements (6); demonstrated stated cases with actual output (3); explanation of the result (1).

Join lines to products and show sale ID, product name and quantity, ordered by sale ID then line ID. Verify names match the referenced IDs. Mark: implementation/artefact meets stated requirements (6); demonstrated stated cases with actual output (3); explanation of the result (1).

Produce Pen=5 and Book=1 units sold using GROUP BY. Explain why grouping by a name alone is unsafe if names can repeat. Mark: implementation/artefact meets stated requirements (6); demonstrated stated cases with actual output (3); explanation of the result (1).

Add Bag without a sale. Use LEFT JOIN and COALESCE so its units sold is 0. Show the difference from the inner join. Mark: implementation/artefact meets stated requirements (6); demonstrated stated cases with actual output (3); explanation of the result (1).

Attempt a line with product_id 999 and show the foreign-key error. Roll back and verify no invalid row remains. Mark: implementation/artefact meets stated requirements (6); demonstrated stated cases with actual output (3); explanation of the result (1).

Store unit_price on sale_lines. Change the current product price and demonstrate that old receipt totals stay unchanged. Explain the intentional duplication. Mark: implementation/artefact meets stated requirements (6); demonstrated stated cases with actual output (3); explanation of the result (1).
Independent verification: new normal case (3), boundary/failure case (3), reproducible commands and observed outputs (2), limitation and repair plan (2).
